speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing a generalized nonpruritic rash along with a recent high fever and a seizure. To understand the cause, can you tell me exactly how long the fever has been present and at what age the seizure occurred?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum) caused by Human Herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6). The clinical presentation of a high fever (40.5°C) followed by a seizure and a subsequent generalized, nonpruritic rash in a 9-month-old infant with no prior serious illness is classic for this condition. The fever typically resolves as the rash appears, which aligns with your description of the rash starting two days after the fever onset.
